question: How many distinct claims (patient control numbers) have been reversed by a payer at least once (an 835 claim payment with claim status 22)? In one row return the number of distinct reversed claims, how many of those claims have any 837 submission in our data, and the total dollars taken back by all reversals (as a positive amount, rounded to 2 decimals).
gold_sql:
select count(distinct r.claim_key) as claims_reversed,
  count(distinct case when exists (select 1 from sem.claims c where c.claim_key=r.claim_key) then r.claim_key end) as reversed_claims_with_837,
  -sum(r.paid_amount) as dollars_taken_back
from sem.remit_claims r where r.is_reversal
answer_key_sql:
select count(distinct e.pcn), count(distinct case when e.pcn in (select pcn from ledger.submissions) then e.pcn end), round(-sum(e.paid),2)
from ledger.events e where status='22'
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Expected answer: 27 reversed claims, 1 with an 837 in the data, $4,008.93 taken back. Claim grain = patient control number across all payers.

question: Gross versus net 835 claim payments by payment month: for each 835 payment month, return gross claim payments (sum of paid on every non-reversal 835 claim payment in the month, including ones later superseded or reversed), reversal takebacks (total of the reversal claim payments, claim status 22, in the month, as a positive amount), the part of those takebacks that reverses a payment from before our data starts (reversals with no earlier non-reversal claim payment from the same payer for the same claim dated before the reversal), net claim payments (gross minus takebacks), and the paid total of today's current adjudications dated in that month. Amounts rounded to 2 decimals; order by month.
gold_sql:
with rc as (
  select r.*, case when r.is_reversal and not exists (
      select 1 from sem.remit_claims o where o.claim_key=r.claim_key and o.payer_key=r.payer_key
        and not o.is_reversal and o.payment_date < r.payment_date) then 1 else 0 end as pre_window_reversal
  from sem.remit_claims r)
select payment_month,
  sum(case when not is_reversal then paid_amount else 0 end) as gross_claim_payments,
  -sum(case when is_reversal then paid_amount else 0 end) as reversal_takebacks,
  -sum(case when pre_window_reversal = 1 then paid_amount else 0 end) as takebacks_of_pre_window_payments,
  sum(paid_amount) as net_claim_payments,
  sum(case when is_current_adjudication then paid_amount else 0 end) as current_paid
from rc group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql:
with e as (select e.*, (status='22' and not exists (select 1 from ledger.events o where o.pcn=e.pcn and o.payer_id=e.payer_id and o.status<>'22' and o.event_number<e.event_number)) prew from ledger.events e)
select date_trunc('month', event_date::date)::date m,
 round(sum(case when status<>'22' then paid else 0 end),2), round(-sum(case when status='22' then paid else 0 end),2),
 round(-sum(case when prew then paid else 0 end),2), round(sum(paid),2), round(sum(case when is_current then paid else 0 end),2)
from e group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Expected answer: 2026-07: 160561.21 / 3828.67 / 3733.98 / 156732.54 / 159852.78; 2026-08: 73342.35 / 180.26 / 53.46 / 73162.09 / 73342.35. The month comes from the 835 payment date of each claim payment. These are claim-payment (CLP04) amounts; provider-level adjustments are excluded.

question: Where do our corrected claims stand with the payer since we sent the correction? For each corrected replacement claim (frequency 7 submission), look at the 835 claim payments from the payer the correction was sent to that are dated on or after the correction's submission date and are not reversals, and take the latest of them (latest payment date). Classify each corrected claim as 'no response yet' (no such 835), 'denied' (that 835 is a denial), 'paid' (paid amount > 0) or 'zero paid, not denied'. Return outcome, number of corrected claims and their total billed charge on the correction (2 decimals), ordered by number of claims descending then outcome.
gold_sql: with c as (select claim_key, payer_key, submission_date, charge_amount from sem.claims where frequency_code='7'), r as (select c.claim_key, c.charge_amount, rc.is_denied, rc.paid_amount, row_number() over (partition by c.claim_key order by rc.payment_date desc, rc.remit_claim_id desc) rn from c left join sem.remit_claims rc on rc.claim_key=c.claim_key and rc.payer_key=c.payer_key and rc.payment_date>=c.submission_date and not rc.is_reversal) select case when paid_amount is null then 'no response yet' when is_denied then 'denied' when paid_amount>0 then 'paid' else 'zero paid, not denied' end outcome, count(*) corrected_claims, round(sum(charge_amount),2) billed_charge from r where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with s as (select s.pcn, s.payer_id, s.submission_date::date sd, c.charge from ledger.submissions s join ledger.claims c using(pcn) where s.frequency='7'), e as (select s.pcn, s.charge, e.paid, e.is_current, a.denied, row_number() over (partition by s.pcn order by e.event_date::date desc, e.event_number desc) rn from s left join ledger.events e on e.pcn=s.pcn and e.payer_id=s.payer_id and e.event_date::date>=s.sd and e.status<>'22' left join ledger.adjudications a on a.pcn=s.pcn and a.payer_id=s.payer_id) select case when paid is null then 'no response yet' when is_current and denied then 'denied' when paid>0 then 'paid' else 'zero paid, not denied' end outcome, count(*) corrected_claims, round(sum(charge),2) billed_charge from e where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Corrected claim = claim_key with a frequency 7 submission (61). Response = non-reversal 835 from the same payer with payment_date >= correction submission date; latest by payment date. Denied uses the 835's is_denied flag.

question: Did correcting claims get us paid more? Take corrected replacement claims (frequency 7 submissions) where the payer the correction went to sent at least one non-reversal 835 claim payment dated before the correction's submission date and at least one dated on or after it. For each such claim, compare the latest non-reversal 835 before the correction with the latest non-reversal 835 on or after it (latest by payment date). In one row return the number of claims, total paid before correction, total paid after correction, and the uplift (after minus before), all dollars rounded to 2 decimals.
gold_sql: with c as (select claim_key, payer_key, submission_date from sem.claims where frequency_code='7'), r as (select c.claim_key, rc.payment_date>=c.submission_date as after_fix, rc.paid_amount, row_number() over (partition by c.claim_key, rc.payment_date>=c.submission_date order by rc.payment_date desc, rc.remit_claim_id desc) rn from c join sem.remit_claims rc on rc.claim_key=c.claim_key and rc.payer_key=c.payer_key and not rc.is_reversal), p as (select claim_key, max(case when not after_fix then paid_amount end) before_paid, max(case when after_fix then paid_amount end) after_paid from r where rn=1 group by 1 having count(*)=2) select count(*) claims, round(sum(before_paid),2) paid_before_correction, round(sum(after_paid),2) paid_after_correction, round(sum(after_paid)-sum(before_paid),2) uplift from p
answer_key_sql: with s as (select pcn, payer_id, submission_date::date sd from ledger.submissions where frequency='7'), r as (select s.pcn, e.event_date::date>=s.sd after_fix, e.paid, row_number() over (partition by s.pcn, e.event_date::date>=s.sd order by e.event_date::date desc, e.event_number desc) rn from s join ledger.events e on e.pcn=s.pcn and e.payer_id=s.payer_id and e.status<>'22'), p as (select pcn, max(case when not after_fix then paid end) b, max(case when after_fix then paid end) a from r where rn=1 group by 1 having count(*)=2) select count(*) claims, round(sum(b),2), round(sum(a),2), round(sum(a)-sum(b),2) from p
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Pairs anchored on each correction's submission date; latest non-reversal 835 on each side, same payer as the correction.

question: Accidental resends: which claims did we send to the same payer more than once as an original claim (frequency code 1 each time, not a correction or void)? In one row return the number of such claims, how many of them received a duplicate-claim denial (CARC 18 duplicate flag) from that payer, how many have a current adjudication from that payer with paid amount > 0, and the total paid on those current adjudications (2 decimals).
gold_sql: with r as (select claim_key, payer_key from sem.claims where frequency_code='1' group by 1,2 having count(*)>1) select count(*) resent_claims, count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims x where x.claim_key=r.claim_key and x.payer_key=r.payer_key and x.is_duplicate_claim_denial)) with_duplicate_denial, count(*) filter (where cur.paid_amount>0) current_paid_claims, round(sum(case when cur.paid_amount>0 then cur.paid_amount else 0 end),2) current_paid from r left join sem.remit_claims cur on cur.claim_key=r.claim_key and cur.payer_key=r.payer_key and cur.is_current_adjudication
answer_key_sql: with r as (select pcn, payer_id from ledger.submissions where frequency='1' group by 1,2 having count(*)>1) select count(*), count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn=r.pcn and e.payer_id=r.payer_id and e.duplicate_denial)), count(*) filter (where a.paid_current>0 and a.remitted_current), round(sum(case when a.remitted_current and a.paid_current>0 then a.paid_current else 0 end),2) from r left join ledger.adjudications a on a.pcn=r.pcn and a.payer_id=r.payer_id
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Resend = >=2 frequency-1 submissions of the same claim_key to the same payer. Current paid from is_current_adjudication of that payer.

question: What prompted our corrected claims? For each corrected replacement claim (frequency 7 submission), find the latest non-reversal 835 claim payment from the payer the correction was sent to that is dated strictly before the correction's submission date. Classify the claim as 'no prior 835', 'prior denial' (that 835 is a denial), 'prior paid' (paid > 0) or 'prior zero paid, not denied'. Return the classification, the number of corrected claims, and the average number of days from that prior 835's payment date to the correction's submission date (1 decimal; null for 'no prior 835'), ordered by number of claims descending then classification.
gold_sql: with c as (select claim_key, payer_key, submission_date from sem.claims where frequency_code='7'), r as (select c.claim_key, c.submission_date, rc.payment_date, rc.is_denied, rc.paid_amount, row_number() over (partition by c.claim_key order by rc.payment_date desc, rc.remit_claim_id desc) rn from c left join sem.remit_claims rc on rc.claim_key=c.claim_key and rc.payer_key=c.payer_key and rc.payment_date<c.submission_date and not rc.is_reversal) select case when paid_amount is null then 'no prior 835' when is_denied then 'prior denial' when paid_amount>0 then 'prior paid' else 'prior zero paid, not denied' end prior_state, count(*) corrected_claims, round(avg(submission_date-payment_date),1) avg_days_prior_835_to_correction from r where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with s as (select pcn, payer_id, submission_date::date sd from ledger.submissions where frequency='7'), dn as (select e.pcn, e.payer_id, e.event_number, (e.status='4' or (e.paid=0 and exists (select 1 from ledger.event_adjustments a join ledger.denial_carcs d using(carc) where a.pcn=e.pcn and a.payer_id=e.payer_id and a.event_number=e.event_number and a.group_code='CO'))) denied from ledger.events e), e as (select s.pcn, s.sd, e.event_date::date ed, e.paid, dn.denied, row_number() over (partition by s.pcn order by e.event_date::date desc, e.event_number desc) rn from s left join ledger.events e on e.pcn=s.pcn and e.payer_id=s.payer_id and e.event_date::date<s.sd and e.status<>'22' left join dn on dn.pcn=e.pcn and dn.payer_id=e.payer_id and dn.event_number=e.event_number) select case when paid is null then 'no prior 835' when denied then 'prior denial' when paid>0 then 'prior paid' else 'prior zero paid, not denied' end, count(*), round(avg(sd-ed),1) from e where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Prior 835 = latest non-reversal 835 from the correction's payer with payment_date < correction submission_date. Denial per glossary (status 4 or $0 with CO reviewed denial CARC).

question: What patient balance is left after all payers? Take every claim with an 837 to its primary payer (payer responsibility 'P') and a current adjudication from that primary payer. The patient's balance after all payers is the patient responsibility (CLP05, missing as 0) on the current adjudication of the claim's secondary payer (the payer billed with payer responsibility 'S') when that secondary has a current adjudication, otherwise the primary's patient responsibility. By the primary payer's class, return the number of claims, the primary-assigned patient responsibility total, and the patient balance after all payers total (2 decimals), ordered by payer class.
gold_sql: with p as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key, payer_class from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P'), s as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='S'), x as (select p.claim_key, p.payer_class, coalesce(rp.patient_responsibility_amount,0) ppr, rs.remit_claim_id is not null has_sec, coalesce(rs.patient_responsibility_amount,0) spr from p join sem.remit_claims rp on rp.claim_key=p.claim_key and rp.payer_key=p.payer_key and rp.is_current_adjudication left join s on s.claim_key=p.claim_key left join sem.remit_claims rs on rs.claim_key=s.claim_key and rs.payer_key=s.payer_key and rs.is_current_adjudication) select payer_class, count(*) claims, round(sum(ppr),2) primary_patient_responsibility, round(sum(case when has_sec then spr else ppr end),2) patient_balance_after_all_payers from x group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with p as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where s.payer_sequence=0), sc as (select distinct pcn, payer_id from ledger.submissions where payer_sequence=1), x as (select p.pcn, p.payer_class, ep.patient_responsibility ppr, es.pcn is not null has_sec, coalesce(es.patient_responsibility,0) spr from p join ledger.events ep on ep.pcn=p.pcn and ep.payer_id=p.payer_id and ep.is_current left join sc on sc.pcn=p.pcn left join ledger.events es on es.pcn=sc.pcn and es.payer_id=sc.payer_id and es.is_current) select payer_class, count(*), round(sum(ppr),2), round(sum(case when has_sec then spr else ppr end),2) from x group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Primary/secondary from 837 payer_responsibility P/S. Current adjudications only. Missing CLP05 treated as 0.

question: How much do we collect per claim from all payers combined? Take claims with an 837 to their primary payer (payer responsibility 'P') and a current adjudication from that primary payer. For each claim add up the paid amount on the current adjudications of every payer that adjudicated it. By the primary payer's class, return the number of claims, total paid by the primary payer, total paid by all other payers, total paid from all payers, and the average total paid per claim (all dollars 2 decimals), ordered by total paid from all payers descending.
gold_sql: with p as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key, payer_class from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P'), x as (select p.claim_key, p.payer_class, rp.paid_amount primary_paid, (select coalesce(sum(o.paid_amount),0) from sem.remit_claims o where o.claim_key=p.claim_key and o.is_current_adjudication and o.payer_key<>p.payer_key) other_paid from p join sem.remit_claims rp on rp.claim_key=p.claim_key and rp.payer_key=p.payer_key and rp.is_current_adjudication) select payer_class, count(*) claims, round(sum(primary_paid),2) primary_paid, round(sum(other_paid),2) other_payers_paid, round(sum(primary_paid+other_paid),2) total_paid, round(avg(primary_paid+other_paid),2) avg_total_paid_per_claim from x group by 1 order by 5 desc
answer_key_sql: with p as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where s.payer_sequence=0), x as (select p.pcn, p.payer_class, a.paid_current pp, (select coalesce(sum(o.paid_current),0) from ledger.adjudications o where o.pcn=p.pcn and o.remitted_current and o.payer_id<>p.payer_id) op from p join ledger.adjudications a on a.pcn=p.pcn and a.payer_id=p.payer_id and a.remitted_current) select payer_class, count(*), round(sum(pp),2), round(sum(op),2), round(sum(pp+op),2), round(avg(pp+op),2) from x group by 1 order by 5 desc
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Population: claim+primary payer (837 P) with a current primary adjudication. Other payers = any other payer's current adjudication for the claim.

question: How much of our secondary-payer money can we trace back to its billing? Look at every claim+payer pair that a payer adjudicated as the secondary payer (an 835 claim payment processed as secondary). By the secondary payer's class, return the number of such claim+payer pairs, how many of them have our 837 to that payer as secondary (payer responsibility 'S') in the data, how many have an 835 from a different payer for the same claim in the data, and the total paid on the secondary's current adjudications (2 decimals), ordered by payer class.
gold_sql: with s as (select claim_key, payer_key, max(payer_class) payer_class from sem.remit_claims where payer_sequence='secondary' group by 1,2) select s.payer_class, count(*) secondary_pairs, count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from sem.claims c where c.claim_key=s.claim_key and c.payer_key=s.payer_key and c.payer_responsibility='S')) with_secondary_837, count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims o where o.claim_key=s.claim_key and o.payer_key<>s.payer_key)) with_other_payer_835, round(sum((select sum(cur.paid_amount) from sem.remit_claims cur where cur.claim_key=s.claim_key and cur.payer_key=s.payer_key and cur.is_current_adjudication)),2) secondary_current_paid from s group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with s as (select pcn, payer_id, payer_class, paid_current, remitted_current from ledger.adjudications where payer_sequence=1) select payer_class, count(*), count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from ledger.submissions x where x.pcn=s.pcn and x.payer_id=s.payer_id and x.payer_sequence=1)), count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from ledger.events o where o.pcn=s.pcn and o.payer_id<>s.payer_id)), round(sum(case when remitted_current then paid_current end),2) from s group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Secondary adjudication = remit_claims payer_sequence 'secondary' (claim status 2); pairs counted once. Other-payer 835 = any 835 for the claim from a different payer.

question: Open secondary AR: which claims have we billed to a secondary payer (an 837 with payer responsibility 'S') that the secondary payer has not adjudicated yet (no current adjudication from that secondary payer)? By the secondary payer's class, return the number of such claims, their billed charge on the latest secondary 837 (2 decimals), and the patient responsibility the primary payer left on its current adjudication for those claims (CLP05, missing as 0; 0 where the primary has no current adjudication; 2 decimals) - the amount we are waiting on the secondary for. Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with s as (select claim_key, payer_key, payer_class, charge_amount, row_number() over (partition by claim_key, payer_key order by submission_date desc, claim_id desc) rn from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='S'), o as (select * from s where rn=1 and not exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims r where r.claim_key=s.claim_key and r.payer_key=s.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication)), p as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P') select o.payer_class, count(*) open_secondary_claims, round(sum(o.charge_amount),2) billed_charge, round(sum(coalesce((select sum(coalesce(rp.patient_responsibility_amount,0)) from p join sem.remit_claims rp on rp.claim_key=p.claim_key and rp.payer_key=p.payer_key and rp.is_current_adjudication where p.claim_key=o.claim_key),0)),2) primary_patient_responsibility from o group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with s as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where s.payer_sequence=1), o as (select s.*, c.charge from s join ledger.claims c using(pcn) where not exists (select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn=s.pcn and e.payer_id=s.payer_id and e.is_current)), p as (select distinct pcn, payer_id from ledger.submissions where payer_sequence=0) select o.payer_class, count(*), round(sum(o.charge),2), round(sum(coalesce((select sum(e.patient_responsibility) from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.is_current where p.pcn=o.pcn),0)),2) from o group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Open = no is_current_adjudication from the secondary payer. Expected = primary (837 P) current adjudication CLP05.

question: How much of each month's 835 cash is for claims billed before our 837 extract begins? Using current adjudications (one per claim and payer), grouped by the month of the 835 payment date, return the payment month, total paid, paid on claims that have no 837 submission in our data at all, and that amount as a percentage of the month's total paid (2 decimals). Dollars rounded to 2 decimals; order by month.
gold_sql: select r.payment_month, round(sum(r.paid_amount),2) total_paid, round(sum(r.paid_amount) filter (where not exists (select 1 from sem.claims c where c.claim_key=r.claim_key)),2) paid_no_837, round(100*sum(r.paid_amount) filter (where not exists (select 1 from sem.claims c where c.claim_key=r.claim_key))/sum(r.paid_amount),2) pct_no_837 from sem.remit_claims r where r.is_current_adjudication group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: select date_trunc('month', e.event_date::date)::date m, round(sum(e.paid),2), round(sum(e.paid) filter (where not exists (select 1 from ledger.submissions s where s.pcn=e.pcn)),2), round(100*sum(e.paid) filter (where not exists (select 1 from ledger.submissions s where s.pcn=e.pcn))/sum(e.paid),2) from ledger.events e where e.is_current group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: No 837 = claim_key absent from sem.claims entirely. Payment month of the current adjudication.

question: How complete is our view of each service month? For service months April 2026 through August 2026 (month of the claim's service-from date), count distinct claims we can see from either an 837 submission or an 835 claim payment, how many of them have at least one 837 in the data, how many are known only from 835s, and the percentage known only from 835s (2 decimals). Order by service month.
gold_sql: with u as (select claim_key, service_month, true has_837 from sem.claims union all select claim_key, service_month, false from sem.remit_claims), k as (select claim_key, min(service_month) service_month, bool_or(has_837) has_837 from u group by 1) select service_month, count(*) claims_seen, count(*) filter (where has_837) with_837, count(*) filter (where not has_837) remit_only, round(100.0*count(*) filter (where not has_837)/count(*),2) pct_remit_only from k where service_month between date '2026-04-01' and date '2026-08-01' group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with u as (select pcn, dos::date dos, true h from ledger.claims union all select pcn, dos::date, false from ledger.events), k as (select pcn, date_trunc('month', min(dos))::date m, bool_or(h) h from u group by 1) select m, count(*), count(*) filter (where h), count(*) filter (where not h), round(100.0*count(*) filter (where not h)/count(*),2) from k where m between date '2026-04-01' and date '2026-08-01' group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Claim universe = union of sem.claims and sem.remit_claims claim_keys; service month from the service-from date (identical across sources).

question: Which payers answered a claim before the earliest 837 we have for it? For each claim and payer, compare the earliest 837 submission to that payer in our data with that payer's earliest 835 claim payment for the claim (any status). Count the claim+payer pairs whose earliest 835 is dated strictly before the earliest 837. Group by the frequency code of that earliest 837 (1 original, 7 replacement, 8 void) and the payer responsibility it was billed with, and return the frequency code, payer responsibility, number of pairs, and the average number of days the 835 preceded the 837 (1 decimal). Order by number of pairs descending, then frequency code, then payer responsibility.
gold_sql: with s as (select claim_key, payer_key, min(submission_date) first_sub from sem.claims group by 1,2), f as (select c.claim_key, c.payer_key, c.frequency_code, c.payer_responsibility from sem.claims c join s on s.claim_key=c.claim_key and s.payer_key=c.payer_key and c.submission_date=s.first_sub qualify row_number() over (partition by c.claim_key, c.payer_key order by c.claim_id)=1), r as (select claim_key, payer_key, min(payment_date) first_pay from sem.remit_claims group by 1,2) select f.frequency_code, f.payer_responsibility, count(*) pairs, round(avg(s.first_sub-r.first_pay),1) avg_days_835_before_837 from s join f using(claim_key,payer_key) join r using(claim_key,payer_key) where r.first_pay<s.first_sub group by 1,2 order by 3 desc,1,2
answer_key_sql: with s as (select pcn, payer_id, min(submission_date::date) fs from ledger.submissions group by 1,2), f as (select x.pcn, x.payer_id, x.frequency, x.payer_sequence from ledger.submissions x join s on s.pcn=x.pcn and s.payer_id=x.payer_id and x.submission_date::date=s.fs qualify row_number() over (partition by x.pcn, x.payer_id order by x.frequency)=1), r as (select pcn, payer_id, min(event_date::date) fp from ledger.events group by 1,2) select f.frequency, case f.payer_sequence when 0 then 'P' else 'S' end, count(*), round(avg(s.fs-r.fp),1) from s join f using(pcn,payer_id) join r using(pcn,payer_id) where r.fp<s.fs group by 1,2 order by 3 desc,1,2
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Per claim+payer: earliest 837 date vs earliest 835 payment date from the same payer. Ties at the earliest submission date broken arbitrarily (none occur).

question: Is August tracking ahead of July? Treat August 2026 as month-to-date through the latest 835 payment date in the data, and compare it with the same day-of-month span of July 2026 (July 1 through the same day number). Using current adjudications (one per claim and payer) dated by 835 payment date, return one row per month with the month (first day), the number of current adjudications, total paid (2 decimals), and the number of distinct claims with paid > 0. Order by month.
gold_sql: with m as (select max(payment_date) d from sem.payments) select r.payment_month, count(*) current_adjudications, round(sum(r.paid_amount),2) total_paid, count(distinct r.claim_key) filter (where r.paid_amount>0) paid_claims from sem.remit_claims r, m where r.is_current_adjudication and ((r.payment_month=date '2026-08-01' and r.payment_date<=m.d) or (r.payment_month=date '2026-07-01' and extract(day from r.payment_date)<=extract(day from m.d))) group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with m as (select max(event_date::date) d from ledger.events) select date_trunc('month', e.event_date::date)::date mo, count(*), round(sum(e.paid),2), count(distinct e.pcn) filter (where e.paid>0) from ledger.events e, m where e.is_current and ((date_trunc('month', e.event_date::date)=date '2026-08-01' and e.event_date::date<=m.d) or (date_trunc('month', e.event_date::date)=date '2026-07-01' and extract(day from e.event_date::date)<=extract(day from m.d))) group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Last payment date in data = 2026-08-18, so July 1-18 vs August 1-18.

question: For the top 5 billed CPT/HCPCS codes by billed charge, compare what we billed with what all payers paid. Billed side: service lines on each claim's latest 837 submission (all frequencies). Paid side: 835 service lines on current adjudications (every payer) of those same claims, attributed to the billed procedure code on the 835 line. Return procedure code, billed lines, billed charge, 835 paid amount, and paid as a percentage of billed charge (2 decimals; dollars 2 decimals). Order by billed charge descending, ties by procedure code.
gold_sql: with b as (select procedure_code, count(*) billed_lines, sum(line_charge_amount) billed_charge from sem.claim_lines where is_latest_submission group by 1), p as (select r.procedure_code, sum(r.line_paid_amount) paid from sem.remit_lines r where r.is_current_adjudication and r.claim_key in (select claim_key from sem.claims) group by 1) select b.procedure_code, b.billed_lines, round(b.billed_charge,2) billed_charge, round(coalesce(p.paid,0),2) paid, round(100*coalesce(p.paid,0)/nullif(b.billed_charge,0),2) paid_pct from b left join p using(procedure_code) order by 3 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with b as (select cpt, count(*) n, sum(charge) ch from ledger.claim_lines group by 1), p as (select el.cpt, sum(el.paid) paid from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) where e.is_current and el.pcn in (select pcn from ledger.submissions) group by 1) select b.cpt, b.n, round(b.ch,2), round(coalesce(p.paid,0),2), round(100*coalesce(p.paid,0)/nullif(b.ch,0),2) from b left join p using(cpt) order by 3 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Billed: latest-submission claim lines. Paid: current-adjudication remit lines (all payers) on claims that have an 837, grouped by billed procedure_code.

question: Which procedures do we bill in multiple units, and how much do payers pay per unit? On 835 service lines of current adjudications (all payers), take each billed CPT/HCPCS code that has at least one line with more than one unit billed. For each, return the procedure code, number of lines, total units billed, total units paid, units cut (billed minus paid), and paid per unit paid (total line paid / total units paid, 2 decimals). Order by total units billed descending, ties by procedure code.
gold_sql: with l as (select procedure_code, coalesce(units_billed, units_paid) ub, units_paid up, line_paid_amount from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication) select procedure_code, count(*) lines, sum(ub)::int units_billed, sum(up)::int units_paid, sum(ub-up)::int units_cut, round(sum(line_paid_amount)/sum(up),2) paid_per_unit_paid from l group by 1 having max(ub)>1 order by 3 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: select el.cpt, count(*), sum(el.units)::int, sum(el.units_paid)::int, sum(el.units-el.units_paid)::int, round(sum(el.paid)/sum(el.units_paid),2) from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) where e.is_current group by 1 having max(el.units)>1 order by 3 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Units billed on 835 lines = SVC07 when present else SVC05 (units paid). Population: all current-adjudication 835 lines.

question: For each billed CPT/HCPCS code with at least 5 service lines denied at line level on current adjudications (835 lines, all payers), what is the most common reviewed denial reason on those denied lines? Count each denied line once per distinct CARC that appears on it under group CO and is a reviewed denial CARC. Return the procedure code, number of denied lines, the most common denial CARC (ties broken by the CARC code in ascending text order), and the number of denied lines carrying it. Order by denied lines descending, then procedure code.
gold_sql: with d as (select remit_line_id, procedure_code from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication and line_is_denied), c as (select distinct d.remit_line_id, d.procedure_code, a.carc_code from d join sem.adjustments a on a.remit_line_id=d.remit_line_id and a.group_code='CO' and a.is_denial_carc), n as (select procedure_code, count(*) denied_lines from d group by 1 having count(*)>=5), m as (select procedure_code, carc_code, count(*) k, row_number() over (partition by procedure_code order by count(*) desc, carc_code) rn from c group by 1,2) select n.procedure_code, n.denied_lines, m.carc_code top_denial_carc, m.k lines_with_top_carc from n join m on m.procedure_code=n.procedure_code and m.rn=1 order by 2 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with d as (select el.pcn, el.payer_id, el.event_number, el.line_number, el.cpt, el.co_carcs from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) where e.is_current and el.denied), c as (select distinct pcn, payer_id, event_number, line_number, cpt, unnest(co_carcs) carc from d), c2 as (select c.* from c join ledger.denial_carcs using(carc)), n as (select cpt, count(*) dl from d group by 1 having count(*)>=5), m as (select cpt, carc, count(*) k, row_number() over (partition by cpt order by count(*) desc, carc) rn from c2 group by 1,2) select n.cpt, n.dl, m.carc, m.k from n join m on m.cpt=n.cpt and m.rn=1 order by 2 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Denied line = line_is_denied on current adjudication lines. CARC counted once per line; CO group and is_denial_carc only.

question: How big are the claims that carry our most common tests? For the 5 CPT/HCPCS codes that appear on the most claims (each claim at its latest 837 submission, counting a claim once per code even if the code is on several lines; ties by procedure code), return the procedure code, number of claims carrying it, the total billed charge of those whole claims, the average whole-claim charge, and the code's own line charge as a percentage of those claims' total charge. Dollars and percentage to 2 decimals. Order by number of claims descending, then procedure code.
gold_sql: with l as (select claim_key, claim_id, procedure_code, line_charge_amount from sem.claim_lines where is_latest_submission), k as (select procedure_code, claim_key, max(claim_id) claim_id, sum(line_charge_amount) code_charge from l group by 1,2), t as (select procedure_code, count(*) claims, sum(c.charge_amount) claim_charge, sum(code_charge) code_charge from k join sem.claims c using(claim_id) group by 1) select procedure_code, claims, round(claim_charge,2) total_claim_charge, round(claim_charge/claims,2) avg_claim_charge, round(100*code_charge/claim_charge,2) code_share_pct from t order by 2 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with k as (select cpt, pcn, sum(charge) cc from ledger.claim_lines group by 1,2), t as (select k.cpt, count(*) n, sum(c.charge) ch, sum(k.cc) cc from k join ledger.claims c using(pcn) group by 1) select cpt, n, round(ch,2), round(ch/n,2), round(100*cc/ch,2) from t order by 2 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Claim grain per code; claim charge from the latest submission's CLM02.

question: What is the effective sequestration rate? On current adjudications (one per claim and payer) that carry any CARC 253 (sequestration) adjustment, by payer class return the number of adjudications, the CARC 253 dollars, the paid amount, and CARC 253 as a percentage of the pre-sequestration payment (paid + CARC 253 dollars), rounded to 3 decimals; dollars to 2 decimals. Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with s as (select remit_claim_id, sum(adjustment_amount) seq from sem.adjustments where carc_code='253' and is_current_adjudication group by 1) select r.payer_class, count(*) adjudications, round(sum(s.seq),2) sequestration, round(sum(r.paid_amount),2) paid, round(100*sum(s.seq)/(sum(r.paid_amount)+sum(s.seq)),3) seq_pct from s join sem.remit_claims r using(remit_claim_id) group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with s as (select a.pcn, a.payer_id, a.event_number, sum(a.amount) seq from ledger.event_adjustments a join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) where e.is_current and a.carc='253' group by all) select p.payer_class, count(*), round(sum(s.seq),2), round(sum(e.paid),2), round(100*sum(s.seq)/(sum(e.paid)+sum(s.seq)),3) from s join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.payers p using(payer_id) group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Claim+payer grain, current adjudications with any CARC 253; group code not restricted (all CO).

question: Which reviewed denial reasons are being pushed to the patient instead of written off? On current adjudications (one per claim and payer), for each reviewed denial CARC that appears under the patient-responsibility group (PR), return the CARC, the number of claim+payer pairs carrying it under PR, the PR dollars for that CARC, how many of those pairs also carry the same CARC under CO, and how many of those pairs are denials under our denial definition. Dollars to 2 decimals; order by number of pairs descending, then CARC.
gold_sql: with pr as (select remit_claim_id, carc_code, sum(adjustment_amount) amt from sem.adjustments where is_current_adjudication and group_code='PR' and is_denial_carc group by 1,2), co as (select distinct remit_claim_id, carc_code from sem.adjustments where is_current_adjudication and group_code='CO') select pr.carc_code, count(*) pairs, round(sum(pr.amt),2) pr_dollars, count(co.remit_claim_id) also_under_co, count(*) filter (where r.is_denied) denied_pairs from pr join sem.remit_claims r using(remit_claim_id) left join co on co.remit_claim_id=pr.remit_claim_id and co.carc_code=pr.carc_code group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with cur as (select pcn, payer_id, event_number from ledger.events where is_current), pr as (select a.pcn, a.payer_id, a.event_number, a.carc, sum(a.amount) amt from ledger.event_adjustments a join cur using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.denial_carcs d on d.carc=a.carc where a.group_code='PR' group by all), co as (select distinct pcn, payer_id, event_number, carc from ledger.event_adjustments where group_code='CO') select pr.carc, count(*), round(sum(pr.amt),2), count(co.pcn), count(*) filter (where ad.denied) from pr join ledger.adjudications ad using(pcn,payer_id) left join co using(pcn,payer_id,event_number,carc) group by 1 order by 2 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Pairs = current remit_claims carrying the CARC under PR; denial per is_denied.

question: How do secondary payers treat the balance the primary left? On current adjudications processed as secondary (claim status 'processed as secondary'), the amount left after the primary is the 835 charge minus the prior-payer adjustment (group OA, CARC 23). By the secondary payer's class, return the number of adjudications, the balance after primary, and the percentages of that balance the secondary paid, wrote off as contractual obligation (all CO-group adjustments), and assigned to the patient (all PR-group adjustments), each rounded to 2 decimals (balance to 2 decimals). Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with r as (select remit_claim_id, payer_class, charge_amount, paid_amount, co_amount, pr_amount from sem.remit_claims where is_current_adjudication and payer_sequence='secondary'), o as (select remit_claim_id, sum(adjustment_amount) oa23 from sem.adjustments where group_code='OA' and carc_code='23' group by 1), x as (select r.*, r.charge_amount-coalesce(o.oa23,0) bal from r left join o using(remit_claim_id)) select payer_class, count(*) adjudications, round(sum(bal),2) balance_after_primary, round(100*sum(paid_amount)/sum(bal),2) paid_pct, round(100*sum(co_amount)/sum(bal),2) co_pct, round(100*sum(pr_amount)/sum(bal),2) pr_pct from x group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with e as (select e.pcn, e.payer_id, e.event_number, e.charge, e.paid, p.payer_class from ledger.events e join ledger.adjudications ad using(pcn,payer_id) join ledger.payers p using(payer_id) where e.is_current and ad.payer_sequence=1 and e.status='2'), a as (select pcn, payer_id, event_number, sum(amount) filter (where group_code='OA' and carc='23') oa23, sum(amount) filter (where group_code='CO') co, sum(amount) filter (where group_code='PR') pr from ledger.event_adjustments group by all), x as (select e.*, e.charge-coalesce(a.oa23,0) bal, coalesce(a.co,0) co, coalesce(a.pr,0) pr from e left join a using(pcn,payer_id,event_number)) select payer_class, count(*), round(sum(bal),2), round(100*sum(paid)/sum(bal),2), round(100*sum(co)/sum(bal),2), round(100*sum(pr)/sum(bal),2) from x group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Secondary = payer_sequence 'secondary' (status 2). Balance = charge - OA-23 (claim+line).

question: How much of the patient responsibility on our current adjudications is ordinary cost sharing versus non-covered services the patient is liable for? On current adjudications (one per claim and payer), split all PR-group adjustment dollars into cost sharing (CARC 1 deductible, 2 coinsurance, 3 copay) and other PR reasons. By payer class, return total PR dollars, cost-sharing dollars, other-PR dollars, other-PR as a percentage of total PR (2 decimals), and the number of claim+payer pairs carrying any other-PR reason. Dollars to 2 decimals; only payer classes with PR dollars; order by payer class.
gold_sql: with a as (select remit_claim_id, payer_class, carc_code, adjustment_amount from sem.adjustments where is_current_adjudication and group_code='PR') select payer_class, round(sum(adjustment_amount),2) pr_total, round(sum(adjustment_amount) filter (where carc_code in ('1','2','3')),2) cost_sharing, round(coalesce(sum(adjustment_amount) filter (where carc_code not in ('1','2','3')),0),2) other_pr, round(100*coalesce(sum(adjustment_amount) filter (where carc_code not in ('1','2','3')),0)/sum(adjustment_amount),2) other_pr_pct, count(distinct remit_claim_id) filter (where carc_code not in ('1','2','3')) pairs_with_other_pr from a group by 1 having sum(adjustment_amount)<>0 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with a as (select a.pcn, a.payer_id, a.carc, a.amount, p.payer_class from ledger.event_adjustments a join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.payers p using(payer_id) where e.is_current and a.group_code='PR') select payer_class, round(sum(amount),2), round(sum(amount) filter (where carc in ('1','2','3')),2), round(coalesce(sum(amount) filter (where carc not in ('1','2','3')),0),2), round(100*coalesce(sum(amount) filter (where carc not in ('1','2','3')),0)/sum(amount),2), count(distinct pcn||'|'||payer_id) filter (where carc not in ('1','2','3')) from a group by 1 having sum(amount)<>0 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Claim and line level PR adjustments on current adjudications; cost sharing = CARC 1/2/3.

question: Are Medicare Advantage plans allowing less than traditional Medicare's lab fee schedule? Use traditional Medicare (payer class 'medicare') as the CLFS benchmark: for each payer-adjudicated procedure code, the benchmark rate is total allowed divided by total paid units across Medicare's current-adjudication 835 lines where Medicare adjudicated the claim as the primary payer, the line is not denied and allowed > 0, rounded to 2 decimals. Then, on Medicare Advantage (payer class 'medicare_advantage') current-adjudication lines adjudicated as primary, not denied, allowed > 0, and with a benchmark for the code, the expected allowed is benchmark x units paid. By Medicare Advantage payer (payer name in upper case), return lines compared, lines whose expected minus allowed is at least $0.02, and the total shortfall (expected minus allowed, summed over those below-expected lines, 2 decimals). Order by total shortfall descending, ties by payer name.
gold_sql: with b as (select adjudicated_procedure_code code, round(sum(line_allowed_amount)/sum(units_paid),2) rate from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication and payer_class='medicare' and payer_sequence='primary' and not line_is_denied and line_allowed_amount>0 group by 1), m as (select upper(r.payer_name) payer, r.line_allowed_amount allowed, b.rate*r.units_paid expected from sem.remit_lines r join b on b.code=r.adjudicated_procedure_code where r.is_current_adjudication and r.payer_class='medicare_advantage' and r.payer_sequence='primary' and not r.line_is_denied and r.line_allowed_amount>0) select payer, count(*) lines_compared, count(*) filter (where expected-allowed>=0.02) lines_below, round(coalesce(sum(expected-allowed) filter (where expected-allowed>=0.02),0),2) shortfall from m group by 1 order by 4 desc, 1
answer_key_sql: with l as (select el.*, a.payer_class, a.payer, a.payer_sequence from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.adjudications a using(pcn,payer_id) where e.is_current and not el.denied and el.allowed>0), b as (select adjudicated_cpt, round(sum(allowed)/sum(units_paid),2) rate from l where payer_class='medicare' and payer_sequence=0 group by 1), m as (select l.payer, l.allowed, b.rate*l.units_paid expected from l join b using(adjudicated_cpt) where l.payer_class='medicare_advantage' and l.payer_sequence=0) select payer, count(*), count(*) filter (where round(expected-allowed,2)>=0.02), round(coalesce(sum(expected-allowed) filter (where round(expected-allowed,2)>=0.02),0),2) from m group by 1 order by 4 desc, 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Benchmark: sum(allowed)/sum(units_paid) on Medicare-primary, non-denied, allowed>0 current lines per adjudicated code.

question: Why are 835 service lines paying zero? On current adjudications (all payers), take the 835 service lines with paid amount $0 and classify each as 'denied' (denied at line level), 'allowed but unpaid' (not denied, allowed amount > 0) or 'no allowance' (not denied, allowed missing or 0). By payer class, return the number of zero-paid lines in each class as three columns (denied, allowed but unpaid, no allowance), the allowed dollars sitting on the allowed-but-unpaid lines (2 decimals), and the zero-paid lines as a percentage of all current-adjudication 835 lines for the payer class (2 decimals). Order by payer class.
gold_sql: select payer_class, count(*) filter (where line_paid_amount=0 and line_is_denied) denied_lines, count(*) filter (where line_paid_amount=0 and not line_is_denied and line_allowed_amount>0) allowed_unpaid_lines, count(*) filter (where line_paid_amount=0 and not line_is_denied and coalesce(line_allowed_amount,0)=0) no_allowance_lines, round(coalesce(sum(line_allowed_amount) filter (where line_paid_amount=0 and not line_is_denied and line_allowed_amount>0),0),2) allowed_unpaid_dollars, round(100.0*count(*) filter (where line_paid_amount=0)/count(*),2) zero_paid_pct from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: select a.payer_class, count(*) filter (where el.paid=0 and el.denied), count(*) filter (where el.paid=0 and not el.denied and el.allowed>0), count(*) filter (where el.paid=0 and not el.denied and coalesce(el.allowed,0)=0), round(coalesce(sum(el.allowed) filter (where el.paid=0 and not el.denied and el.allowed>0),0),2), round(100.0*count(*) filter (where el.paid=0)/count(*),2) from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.adjudications a using(pcn,payer_id) where e.is_current group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Line grain on current adjudications; NULL allowed treated as no allowance.

question: What is our open primary AR worth at Medicare rates rather than at billed charges? Open primary AR = claims whose latest 837 submission is not a void (frequency 8) and whose primary payer (payer responsibility 'P') has no current adjudication. Value each billed service line on the claim's latest submission at the Medicare benchmark for its billed procedure code: total allowed / total paid units on traditional Medicare (payer class 'medicare') current-adjudication 835 lines where Medicare was the primary payer, the line is not denied and allowed > 0, rounded to 2 decimals, times the units billed on the 837 line (lines whose code has no benchmark are valued at 0). By the primary payer's class, return open claims, billed charge, benchmark value, and benchmark value as a percentage of billed charge (dollars and percentage 2 decimals). Order by billed charge descending.
gold_sql: with b as (select procedure_code, round(sum(line_allowed_amount)/sum(units_paid),2) rate from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication and payer_class='medicare' and payer_sequence='primary' and not line_is_denied and line_allowed_amount>0 group by 1), p as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key, payer_class from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P'), o as (select p.claim_key, p.payer_class from p join sem.claims l on l.claim_key=p.claim_key and l.is_latest_submission and l.frequency_code<>'8' where not exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims r where r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication)), v as (select o.claim_key, o.payer_class, sum(cl.line_charge_amount) charge, sum(coalesce(b.rate,0)*cl.units_billed) value from o join sem.claim_lines cl on cl.claim_key=o.claim_key and cl.is_latest_submission left join b on b.procedure_code=cl.procedure_code group by 1,2) select payer_class, count(*) open_claims, round(sum(charge),2) billed_charge, round(sum(value),2) benchmark_value, round(100*sum(value)/sum(charge),2) value_pct_of_charge from v group by 1 order by 3 desc
answer_key_sql: with b as (select el.cpt, round(sum(el.allowed)/sum(el.units_paid),2) rate from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.adjudications a using(pcn,payer_id) where e.is_current and a.payer_class='medicare' and a.payer_sequence=0 and not el.denied and el.allowed>0 group by 1), p as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where s.payer_sequence=0), o as (select p.pcn, p.payer_class from p join ledger.claims c using(pcn) where not c.voided and not exists (select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.is_current)), v as (select o.pcn, o.payer_class, sum(cl.charge) ch, sum(coalesce(b.rate,0)*cl.units) val from o join ledger.claim_lines cl using(pcn) left join b using(cpt) group by 1,2) select payer_class, count(*), round(sum(ch),2), round(sum(val),2), round(100*sum(val)/sum(ch),2) from v group by 1 order by 3 desc

question: How do payer classes price our tests relative to the Medicare lab fee schedule? Build the CLFS benchmark per payer-adjudicated procedure code as total allowed / total paid units on traditional Medicare (payer class 'medicare') current-adjudication 835 lines where Medicare was the primary payer, the line is not denied and allowed > 0, rounded to 2 decimals. Then, for every other payer class, take current-adjudication 835 lines where that payer adjudicated as primary, not denied, allowed > 0 and the adjudicated code has a benchmark. Return payer class, lines, total allowed, total benchmark-expected allowed (benchmark x units paid), and allowed as a percentage of benchmark (2 decimals; dollars 2 decimals). Order by the percentage descending.
gold_sql: with b as (select adjudicated_procedure_code code, round(sum(line_allowed_amount)/sum(units_paid),2) rate from sem.remit_lines where is_current_adjudication and payer_class='medicare' and payer_sequence='primary' and not line_is_denied and line_allowed_amount>0 group by 1) select r.payer_class, count(*) lines, round(sum(r.line_allowed_amount),2) allowed, round(sum(b.rate*r.units_paid),2) expected, round(100*sum(r.line_allowed_amount)/sum(b.rate*r.units_paid),2) pct_of_benchmark from sem.remit_lines r join b on b.code=r.adjudicated_procedure_code where r.is_current_adjudication and r.payer_class<>'medicare' and r.payer_sequence='primary' and not r.line_is_denied and r.line_allowed_amount>0 group by 1 order by 5 desc
answer_key_sql: with l as (select el.*, a.payer_class, a.payer_sequence from ledger.event_lines el join ledger.events e using(pcn,payer_id,event_number) join ledger.adjudications a using(pcn,payer_id) where e.is_current and not el.denied and el.allowed>0), b as (select adjudicated_cpt, round(sum(allowed)/sum(units_paid),2) rate from l where payer_class='medicare' and payer_sequence=0 group by 1) select payer_class, count(*), round(sum(allowed),2), round(sum(rate*units_paid),2), round(100*sum(allowed)/sum(rate*units_paid),2) from l join b using(adjudicated_cpt) where payer_class<>'medicare' and payer_sequence=0 group by 1 order by 5 desc
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Primary-only lines on both sides; benchmark per adjudicated code.

question: How long does it take for a claim to settle with a payer when it takes more than one 835? For claim+payer pairs that received at least two 835 claim payments from that payer and have a current adjudication, measure the days from the pair's earliest 835 payment date to the payment date of its current adjudication. By payer class, return the number of pairs, the median days and the 90th percentile days (continuous/interpolated percentiles, 1 decimal), and how many pairs have a later 835 after the current adjudication. Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with p as (select claim_key, payer_key, max(payer_class) payer_class, min(payment_date) first_pay, max(payment_date) last_pay, count(*) n from sem.remit_claims group by 1,2 having count(*)>=2), x as (select p.*, c.payment_date cur_pay from p join sem.remit_claims c on c.claim_key=p.claim_key and c.payer_key=p.payer_key and c.is_current_adjudication) select payer_class, count(*) pairs, round(quantile_cont(cur_pay-first_pay,0.5),1) median_days, round(quantile_cont(cur_pay-first_pay,0.9),1) p90_days, count(*) filter (where last_pay>cur_pay) pairs_with_later_835 from x group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with p as (select pcn, payer_id, min(event_date::date) fp, max(event_date::date) lp from ledger.events group by 1,2 having count(*)>=2), x as (select p.*, e.event_date::date cp, py.payer_class from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.is_current join ledger.payers py on py.payer_id=p.payer_id) select payer_class, count(*), round(quantile_cont(cp-fp,0.5),1), round(quantile_cont(cp-fp,0.9),1), count(*) filter (where lp>cp) from x group by 1 order by 1

question: How long is the full coordination-of-benefits cycle? For claims billed to both a primary payer (837 payer responsibility 'P') and a secondary payer (payer responsibility 'S') where both payers have a current adjudication, measure days from the primary's current adjudication payment date to the secondary's current adjudication payment date, and separately days from the earliest 837 submission of the claim (any payer) to the secondary's current adjudication. By the secondary payer's class, return the number of claims, the median and maximum of the primary-to-secondary days, and the median submission-to-secondary days (medians interpolated, 1 decimal). Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with p as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P'), s as (select distinct claim_key, payer_key, payer_class from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='S'), f as (select claim_key, min(submission_date) fs from sem.claims group by 1), x as (select s.payer_class, rp.payment_date pd, rs.payment_date sd, f.fs from p join s using(claim_key) join f using(claim_key) join sem.remit_claims rp on rp.claim_key=p.claim_key and rp.payer_key=p.payer_key and rp.is_current_adjudication join sem.remit_claims rs on rs.claim_key=s.claim_key and rs.payer_key=s.payer_key and rs.is_current_adjudication) select payer_class, count(*) claims, round(quantile_cont(sd-pd,0.5),1) median_primary_to_secondary, max(sd-pd) max_primary_to_secondary, round(quantile_cont(sd-fs,0.5),1) median_submission_to_secondary from x group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with p as (select distinct pcn, payer_id from ledger.submissions where payer_sequence=0), s as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where payer_sequence=1), f as (select pcn, min(submission_date::date) fs from ledger.submissions group by 1), x as (select s.payer_class, ep.event_date::date pd, es.event_date::date sd, f.fs from p join s using(pcn) join f using(pcn) join ledger.events ep on ep.pcn=p.pcn and ep.payer_id=p.payer_id and ep.is_current join ledger.events es on es.pcn=s.pcn and es.payer_id=s.payer_id and es.is_current) select payer_class, count(*), round(quantile_cont(sd-pd,0.5),1), max(sd-pd), round(quantile_cont(sd-fs,0.5),1) from x group by 1 order by 1
source: opus-authored, single author: gold over sem.* matches its own ledger answer key
interpretation: Pairs by 837 P/S; earliest submission any payer.

question: Which open primary claims are overdue relative to how fast that payer class normally answers? Step 1: for each claim and its primary payer (837 payer responsibility 'P'), turnaround is the days from the earliest primary 837 submission to that payer to the earliest 835 claim payment from that payer dated on or after that submission; per primary payer class take the 90th percentile turnaround (continuous/interpolated). Step 2: open primary claims are those whose latest submission is not a void (frequency 8) and whose primary payer has no current adjudication; age is days from the earliest primary submission to that payer through the latest 835 payment date in the data. By payer class return the p90 turnaround (1 decimal), the number of open claims, and the number and billed charge (charge on the claim's earliest primary submission, 2 decimals) of open claims older than the p90. Order by payer class.
gold_sql: with p as (select claim_key, payer_key, max(payer_class) payer_class, min(submission_date) fs, arg_min(charge_amount, submission_date) ch from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P' group by 1,2), t as (select p.payer_class, min(r.payment_date)-p.fs ndays from p join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.payment_date>=p.fs group by p.claim_key, p.payer_key, p.payer_class, p.fs), q as (select payer_class, quantile_cont(ndays,0.9) p90 from t group by 1), as_of_date as (select max(payment_date) d from sem.payments), o as (select p.*, (select d from as_of_date)-p.fs age from p join sem.claims l on l.claim_key=p.claim_key and l.is_latest_submission and l.frequency_code<>'8' where not exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims r where r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication)) select q.payer_class, round(q.p90,1) p90_turnaround_days, count(o.claim_key) open_claims, count(o.claim_key) filter (where o.age>q.p90) open_past_p90, round(coalesce(sum(o.ch) filter (where o.age>q.p90),0),2) charge_past_p90 from q left join o on o.payer_class=q.payer_class group by q.payer_class, q.p90 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with p as (select s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class, min(s.submission_date::date) fs from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using(payer_id) where s.payer_sequence=0 group by all), t as (select p.payer_class, min(e.event_date::date)-p.fs ndays from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.event_date::date>=p.fs group by p.pcn, p.payer_id, p.payer_class, p.fs), q as (select payer_class, quantile_cont(ndays,0.9) p90 from t group by 1), as_of_date as (select max(event_date::date) d from ledger.events), o as (select p.*, c.charge ch, (select d from as_of_date)-p.fs age from p join ledger.claims c using(pcn) where not c.voided and not exists (select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.is_current)) select q.payer_class, round(q.p90,1), count(o.pcn), count(o.pcn) filter (where o.age>q.p90), round(coalesce(sum(o.ch) filter (where o.age>q.p90),0),2) from q left join o on o.payer_class=q.payer_class group by q.payer_class, q.p90 order by 1

interpretation: As-of = max payment date (2026-08-18). Charge from earliest primary submission (charges identical across submissions in this data).

question: Do payers deny faster than they pay? For each claim and its primary payer (837 payer responsibility 'P'), take the earliest primary 837 submission to that payer and the first 835 claim payment from that payer dated on or after it (ties on the same date: the 835 with the higher paid amount). Classify that first response as 'denied' (the 835 is a denial), 'paid' (paid > 0) or 'zero paid, not denied'. For each class return the number of claims and the 25th, 50th and 90th percentile days from submission to that first response (continuous/interpolated, 1 decimal). Order by number of claims descending.
gold_sql: with p as (select claim_key, payer_key, min(submission_date) fs from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P' group by 1,2), f as (select p.claim_key, r.payment_date-p.fs ndays, r.is_denied, r.paid_amount, row_number() over (partition by p.claim_key, p.payer_key order by r.payment_date, r.paid_amount desc) rn from p join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.payment_date>=p.fs) select case when is_denied then 'denied' when paid_amount>0 then 'paid' else 'zero paid, not denied' end first_response, count(*) claims, round(quantile_cont(ndays,0.25),1) p25_days, round(quantile_cont(ndays,0.5),1) p50_days, round(quantile_cont(ndays,0.9),1) p90_days from f where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc
answer_key_sql: with p as (select pcn, payer_id, min(submission_date::date) fs from ledger.submissions where payer_sequence=0 group by 1,2), dn as (select e.pcn, e.payer_id, e.event_number, e.status<>'22' and (e.status='4' or (e.paid=0 and exists (select 1 from ledger.event_adjustments a join ledger.denial_carcs d using(carc) where a.pcn=e.pcn and a.payer_id=e.payer_id and a.event_number=e.event_number and a.group_code='CO'))) denied from ledger.events e), f as (select p.pcn, e.event_date::date-p.fs nd, dn.denied, e.paid, row_number() over (partition by p.pcn, p.payer_id order by e.event_date::date, e.paid desc) rn from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.event_date::date>=p.fs join dn on dn.pcn=e.pcn and dn.payer_id=e.payer_id and dn.event_number=e.event_number) select case when denied then 'denied' when paid>0 then 'paid' else 'zero paid, not denied' end, count(*), round(quantile_cont(nd,0.25),1), round(quantile_cont(nd,0.5),1), round(quantile_cont(nd,0.9),1) from f where rn=1 group by 1 order by 2 desc

question: Does billing lag hurt outcomes? Bucket claims by days from service-from date to the earliest primary 837 submission (payer responsibility 'P') in our data: '0-3', '4-7', '8-14', '15+'. For each bucket, among claims whose primary payer has a current adjudication, return the number of claims billed in the bucket, the number with a current primary adjudication, the primary denial rate (denied current primary adjudications / current primary adjudications, as a percentage, 2 decimals) and the primary paid-to-charge ratio (current primary paid / 835 charge on those adjudications, percentage, 2 decimals). Order by bucket in the order listed.
gold_sql: with p as (select claim_key, payer_key, min(service_date_from) dos, min(submission_date) fs from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P' group by 1,2), b as (select p.*, case when fs-dos<=3 then '0-3' when fs-dos<=7 then '4-7' when fs-dos<=14 then '8-14' else '15+' end bucket, r.remit_claim_id, r.is_denied, r.paid_amount, r.charge_amount from p left join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication) select bucket, count(*) claims_billed, count(remit_claim_id) adjudicated, round(100.0*count(*) filter (where is_denied)/count(remit_claim_id),2) denial_rate_pct, round(100*sum(paid_amount)/sum(charge_amount),2) paid_to_charge_pct from b group by 1 order by case bucket when '0-3' then 1 when '4-7' then 2 when '8-14' then 3 else 4 end
answer_key_sql: with p as (select s.pcn, s.payer_id, min(s.submission_date::date) fs from ledger.submissions s where payer_sequence=0 group by 1,2), b as (select p.*, c.dos::date dos, case when fs-c.dos::date<=3 then '0-3' when fs-c.dos::date<=7 then '4-7' when fs-c.dos::date<=14 then '8-14' else '15+' end bucket, e.pcn epcn, a.denied, e.paid, e.charge from p join ledger.claims c using(pcn) left join ledger.events e on e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.is_current left join ledger.adjudications a on a.pcn=p.pcn and a.payer_id=p.payer_id) select bucket, count(*), count(epcn), round(100.0*count(*) filter (where epcn is not null and denied)/count(epcn),2), round(100*sum(paid)/sum(charge),2) from b group by 1 order by case bucket when '0-3' then 1 when '4-7' then 2 when '8-14' then 3 else 4 end

question: Which ordering providers bring us the most cash per order? For each referring provider NPI (from each claim's latest 837 submission, excluding claims whose latest submission is a void), among providers with at least 20 such claims, compute collected per claim = total paid on the current adjudications of every payer for those claims divided by the provider's number of claims (including claims with no payment yet). Return the top 5 providers by collected per claim (ties by NPI ascending) with NPI, claims, claims with any current adjudication, total collected, and collected per claim (dollars 2 decimals).
gold_sql: with c as (select claim_key, referring_npi from sem.claims where is_latest_submission and frequency_code<>'8'), r as (select claim_key, sum(paid_amount) paid from sem.remit_claims where is_current_adjudication group by 1), x as (select c.referring_npi, count(*) claims, count(r.claim_key) remitted, coalesce(sum(r.paid),0) collected from c left join r using(claim_key) group by 1 having count(*)>=20) select referring_npi, claims, remitted claims_with_current_adjudication, round(collected,2) total_collected, round(collected/claims,2) collected_per_claim from x order by collected/claims desc, referring_npi

question: Within each payer class, which procedures have the worst line-level denial rate? Use 835 service lines on current adjudications (all payers), grouped by payer class and billed procedure code, keeping codes with at least 30 lines in that payer class. Line denial rate = lines denied at line level / lines, as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals. question: Is speed-to-cash improving week over week? For each week return the number of claims, how many received an 835 from their primary payer with paid amount > 0 dated within 21 days after the service date (service date + 21 or earlier), and that as a percentage of the week's claims (2 decimals). Order by week.
gold_sql: with p as (select claim_key, payer_key, min(service_date_from) dos from sem.claims where payer_responsibility='P' group by 1,2), m as (select max(payment_date) d from sem.payments), w as (select p.*, date_trunc('week', dos)::date wk, exists (select 1 from sem.remit_claims r where r.claim_key=p.claim_key and r.payer_key=p.payer_key and r.paid_amount>0 and r.payment_date<=p.dos+21) paid21 from p) select wk week_start, count(*) claims, count(*) filter (where paid21) paid_within_21_days, round(100.0*count(*) filter (where paid21)/count(*),2) pct from w, m where wk>=date '2026-06-29' and wk+6+21<=m.d group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with p as (select distinct s.pcn, s.payer_id, c.dos::date dos from ledger.submissions s join ledger.claims c using(pcn) where s.payer_sequence=0), m as (select max(event_date::date) d from ledger.events), w as (select p.*, date_trunc('week', dos)::date wk, exists (select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn=p.pcn and e.payer_id=p.payer_id and e.paid>0 and e.event_date::date<=p.dos+21) paid21 from p) select wk, count(*), count(*) filter (where paid21), round(100.0*count(*) filter (where paid21)/count(*),2) from w, m where wk>=date '2026-06-29' and wk+6+21<=m.d group by 1 order by 1

question: For each payer class and 835 payment month, among current adjudications only (one row per claim and payer), how many paid exactly $0 but are not denials? $0 paid alone is not a denial: a denial is a recorded denial (claim status 4) or the signal rule ($0 paid, not a reversal, with a CO adjustment whose CARC is on the reviewed denial list). By payer class and bucket, return the number of paid adjudications and the paid dollars (2 decimals). This includes 835s for claims billed before the data window. Order by payer class, then bucket.
gold_sql: select payer_class, case when payment_date - service_date_from <= 14 then '0-14' when payment_date - service_date_from <= 30 then '15-30' when payment_date - service_date_from <= 45 then '31-45' else '46+' end age_bucket, count(*) paid_adjudications, round(sum(paid_amount), 2) paid from sem.remit_claims where is_current_adjudication and paid_amount > 0 and service_date_from is not null group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2
answer_key_sql: select a.payer_class, case when e.event_date::date - e.dos::date <= 14 then '0-14' when e.event_date::date - e.dos::date <= 30 then '15-30' when e.event_date::date - e.dos::date <= 45 then '31-45' else '46+' end age_bucket, count(*) paid_adjudications, round(sum(e.paid), 2) paid from ledger.events e join ledger.adjudications a using (pcn, payer_id) where e.is_current and e.paid > 0 and e.dos is not null group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2
alt_sql: select payer_class, case when payment_date - service_date_from <= 14 then '0-14' when payment_date - service_date_from <= 30 then '15-30' when payment_date - service_date_from <= 45 then '31-45' else '46+' end, count(*), sum(paid_amount) from sem.remit_claims where is_current_adjudication and paid_amount > 0 and service_date_from is not null group by 1, 2

question: Which primary payers pay within 21 days of our first bill? Take each claim's primary payer (payer_responsibility = 'P' on the 837) and its first 837 submission date to that payer. Keep claims that have a current adjudication from that payer. A claim counts as paid within 21 days only when that adjudication paid more than zero and the payment date is no more than 21 days after the first submission. For payers with at least 25 such current adjudications, return the payer name, the number of current adjudications, how many were paid within 21 days, and that share as a percent rounded to 1 decimal. Order by the percent descending, then payer name.
gold_sql: with p as ( select claim_key, payer_key, payer_name, min(submission_date) first_sub from sem.claims where payer_responsibility = 'P' group by all), d as ( select p.payer_name, (r.paid_amount > 0 and r.payment_date - p.first_sub <= 21) within_21 from p join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key = p.claim_key and r.payer_key = p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication) select payer_name, count(*) current_primary, count(*) filter (where within_21) paid_within_21, round(100.0 * avg(within_21::int), 1) pct_paid_within_21 from d group by 1 having count(*) >= 25 order by pct_paid_within_21 desc, payer_name
answer_key_sql: with p as ( select s.pcn, s.payer_id, min(s.submission_date::date) first_sub from ledger.submissions s where s.payer_sequence = 0 group by all), d as ( select array_to_string(list_transform(string_split(lower(py.payer), ' '), lambda x: upper(x[1]) || x[2:]), ' ') payer_name, (e.paid > 0 and e.event_date::date - p.first_sub <= 21) within_21 from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn = p.pcn and e.payer_id = p.payer_id and e.is_current join ledger.payers py on py.payer_id = p.payer_id) select payer_name, count(*) current_primary, count(*) filter (where within_21) paid_within_21, round(100.0 * avg(within_21::int), 1) pct_paid_within_21 from d group by 1 having count(*) >= 25 order by pct_paid_within_21 desc, payer_name
alt_sql: with p as ( select claim_key, payer_key, payer_name, min(submission_date) first_sub from sem.claims where payer_responsibility = 'P' group by all), d as ( select p.payer_name, (r.paid_amount > 0 and r.payment_date - p.first_sub <= 21) within_21 from p join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key = p.claim_key and r.payer_key = p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication) select payer_name, count(*), sum(within_21::int), round(100.0 * avg(within_21::int), 1) from d group by 1 having count(*) >= 25

question: For claims whose primary payer (payer_responsibility = 'P') has a current adjudication with paid amount greater than zero, bucket the days from the first 837 submission to that payer until that payment date: 0-7, 8-14, 15-30, and 31 or more. By payer class and bucket, return paid claims and paid dollars (2 decimals). Claims with no primary 837 in the data are excluded. Order by payer class, then bucket.

answer_key_sql: with p as ( select s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class, min(s.submission_date::date) first_sub from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using (payer_id) where s.payer_sequence = 0 group by all) select p.payer_class, case when e.event_date::date - p.first_sub <= 7 then '0-7' when e.event_date::date - p.first_sub <= 14 then '8-14' when e.event_date::date - p.first_sub <= 30 then '15-30' else '31+' end age_bucket, count(*) paid_claims, round(sum(e.paid), 2) paid from p join ledger.events e on e.pcn = p.pcn and e.payer_id = p.payer_id and e.is_current where e.paid > 0 group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2

question: What does secondary billing look like by the secondary payer's class? A secondary bill is an 837 with payer_responsibility = 'S'. Return, by secondary payer class: claims billed, how many have a current adjudication from that secondary payer, paid dollars on those current adjudications (0 when none, 2 decimals), and the median days from that earliest secondary submission to the current payment date among adjudications with paid amount greater than zero (1 decimal; null when the class has none). gold_sql: with s as ( select claim_key, payer_key, payer_class, submission_date from ( select claim_key, payer_key, payer_class, submission_date, row_number() over (partition by claim_key, payer_key order by submission_date, claim_id) rn from sem.claims where payer_responsibility = 'S') t where rn = 1) select s.payer_class, count(*) billed_claims, count(r.remit_claim_id) with_current_adjudication, round(coalesce(sum(r.paid_amount), 0), 2) current_paid, round(median(r.payment_date - s.submission_date) filter (where r.paid_amount > 0), 1) median_days_to_pay from s left join sem.remit_claims r on r.claim_key = s.claim_key and r.payer_key = s.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with s as ( select pcn, payer_id, payer_class, submission_date from ( select s.pcn, s.payer_id, py.payer_class, s.submission_date::date submission_date, row_number() over (partition by s.pcn, s.payer_id order by s.submission_date, s.payer_id) rn from ledger.submissions s join ledger.payers py using (payer_id) where s.payer_sequence = 1) t where rn = 1) select s.payer_class, count(*) billed_claims, count(e.pcn) with_current_adjudication, round(coalesce(sum(e.paid), 0), 2) current_paid, round(median(e.event_date::date - s.submission_date) filter (where e.paid > 0), 1) median_days_to_pay from s left join ledger.events e on e.pcn = s.pcn and e.payer_id = s.payer_id and e.is_current group by 1 order by 1

gold_sql: with rev as ( select distinct claim_key, payer_key from sem.remit_claims where is_reversal) select r.payer_class, count(*) current_adjudications, count(*) filter (where rev.claim_key is not null) pairs_with_a_reversal, round(sum(r.paid_amount), 2) paid, round(coalesce(sum(r.paid_amount) filter (where rev.claim_key is not null), 0), 2) paid_on_reversed_pairs from sem.remit_claims r left join rev using (claim_key, payer_key) where r.is_current_adjudication group by 1 order by 1
answer_key_sql: with rev as ( select distinct pcn, payer_id from ledger.events where status = '22') select a.payer_class, count(*) current_adjudications, count(*) filter (where rev.pcn is not null) pairs_with_a_reversal, round(sum(e.paid), 2) paid, round(coalesce(sum(e.paid) filter (where rev.pcn is not null), 0), 2) paid_on_reversed_pairs from ledger.events e join ledger.adjudications a using (pcn, payer_id) left join rev using (pcn, payer_id) where e.is_current group by 1 order by 1

question: Open primary AR, aged in 30-day buckets as of the latest 835 payment date in the data (the maximum payment_date on sem.payments). A claim is open when its latest 837 submission is not a void (frequency 8) and its primary payer (payer_responsibility = 'P') has no current adjudication, either because nothing came back or because the latest event was a reversal. Age is that as-of date minus the first 837 submission date to the primary payer. Buckets are 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 91 or more. By payer class and bucket, return open claims and billed charge from the claim's latest submission (2 decimals). Order by payer class, then bucket.
gold_sql: with cutoff as (select max(payment_date) as_of from sem.payments), p as ( select claim_key, payer_key, payer_class, min(submission_date) first_sub from sem.claims where payer_responsibility = 'P' group by all), l as ( select claim_key, frequency_code, charge_amount from sem.claims where is_latest_submission), o as ( select p.payer_class, l.charge_amount, (select as_of from cutoff) - p.first_sub as age_days from p join l using (claim_key) where l.frequency_code <> '8' and not exists ( select 1 from sem.remit_claims r where r.claim_key = p.claim_key and r.payer_key = p.payer_key and r.is_current_adjudication)) select payer_class, case when age_days <= 30 then '0-30' when age_days <= 60 then '31-60' when age_days <= 90 then '61-90' else '91+' end age_bucket, count(*) open_claims, round(sum(charge_amount), 2) open_charge from o group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2
answer_key_sql: with cutoff as (select max(event_date::date) as_of from ledger.events), p as ( select pcn, payer_id, min(submission_date::date) first_sub from ledger.submissions where payer_sequence = 0 group by all), o as ( select py.payer_class, c.charge, (select as_of from cutoff) - p.first_sub as age_days from p join ledger.claims c using (pcn) join ledger.payers py using (payer_id) where not c.voided and not exists ( select 1 from ledger.events e where e.pcn = p.pcn and e.payer_id = p.payer_id and e.is_current)) select payer_class, case when age_days <= 30 then '0-30' when age_days <= 60 then '31-60' when age_days <= 90 then '61-90' else '91+' end age_bucket, count(*) open_claims, round(sum(charge), 2) open_charge from o group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2
